title: Operational readiness
summary: Make the remote service deployable, observable, supportable, and safe before compatible clients ship.
produces: TLS, HSTS, proxy, and real-client rate-limit conformance
Alerts, retention proof, break-glass authorization, and lost-ID support

conditions: A new operator can deploy from the documentation.
Plaintext requests are refused rather than redirected or proxied.
Proxy address handling and every rate limit are proven against running configuration.
Alerting, retention proof, break-glass authorization, and lost-ID support are exercised.
The compatible service is deployed before beta and public client distribution.
completion.summary: Athenaeum is deployed from the published runbook with its loopback-only Apache topology, live proxy conformance, human-received operational alerts, observed retention cleanup, authorized break-glass audit, and lost-ID support path proven before a compatible client ships.
evidence: PR #1183 delivered the container, Apache deployment, smoke harness, operations runbook, alerting, retention, break-glass, and support procedures; PR #1220 persisted the corrections proven on the live deployment.
.github/tracking/adr-004/evidence/W16.md records the deployed revision and image, loopback listener, plaintext refusal, HTTPS/HSTS behavior, and the passing live proxy and rate-limit conformance run.
The live quota exercise accepted 250 unique 1 MiB blobs, refused blob 251 with HTTP 507, emitted quota_exhaustion, and delivered the matching alert email to the human recipient.

The live hourly sweep emitted and delivered sweep_failure under an injected filesystem error; after restoring permissions, the durable retry removed every database row and the epoch directory, while count-only scans found no credential, sync-ID-shaped, or test-content log entries.

The public PR #1211 approval preceded one end-to-end break-glass read; the separate audit database gained exactly one matching row, the ordinary database had no break-glass table, and the disposable store was removed.
The lost-ID process was exercised against a real disposable store whose raw ID was no longer available: no recovery or access path existed, and the support result required creation of a new store.
The service was deployed before any user-facing compatible client: W13 and W14 remained incomplete and no Device Sync settings surface was distributed.
